A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FACTS and share the core framework, theoretical analysis, and original experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original multivariate forecasting and CLEVRER experiments, permutation tests, and encoder/factor-count ablations in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds OBJ3D, MOVi-A, and METR-LA evaluations, alongside additional sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The core recurrence and attention router remain intact. v2 adds a graph-task adaptation that masks routing used to construct selective SSM parameters (Appendix C.4), and a reconstruction configuration with the predictive residual disabled (Appendix C.3). These are limited procedural adaptations; expanded residual documentation does not establish when it entered the existing experiments.

E1.justification: v2 adds OBJ3D slot-dynamics prediction, MOVi-A reconstruction-based object discovery, and METR-LA graph-node forecasting. This extends coverage to reconstruction objectives and graph-structured sensor inputs while retaining the nine forecasting datasets and CLEVRER experiments.

E2.justification: New comparisons include SAVi and OC-SlotSSM for MOVi-A reconstruction (Table 3) and thirteen graph-forecasting baselines, including DCRNN, STGCN, MegaCRN, and TESTAM (Table 4). The original forecasting and slot-prediction comparator sets remain unchanged; extending the latter to OBJ3D is coverage expansion.

E3.justification: v2 introduces reconstruction evaluation with the residual predictor disabled and one-hour, 12-step METR-LA forecasting measured by RMSE, MAE, and MAPE. New analyses vary chunk sizes and the slot count of a fixed trained model at testing. The retained MTS input/prediction lengths and CLEVRER slot-dynamics rollout protocol remain the same.

E4.justification: v2 adds recurrent-versus-parallel chunk-size analysis on Electricity (Figure 3) and test-time slot-count sensitivity on MOVi-A (Figure 4). These examine computational configuration and inference-time factor capacity. The original encoder and training-time factor-count ablations are retained as Tables 6–7 in Appendix D, rather than removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds and error bars of twice the standard deviation for Figure 2, plus standard-error summaries in the retained ablation tables. v2 introduces no additional uncertainty-reporting procedure or stated increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds OBJ3D LPIPS results, MOVi-A segmentation results, METR-LA forecasting scores, and new sensitivity curves. FACTS obtains 0.07 OBJ3D LPIPS and 0.75/0.60 MOVi-A FG-ARI/mIoU. Retained forecasting entries also change: Table 1 Exchange MSE changes from 0.355 to 0.342 and Traffic MSE from 0.470 to 0.472. CLEVRER quantitative results remain unchanged, while several original qualitative examples are replaced.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–2, Theorems 1–2, and the Appendix B proofs remain substantively unchanged. The expanded transition-product notation and explicit all-ones identity clarify the existing elementwise recurrence without changing its theoretical content.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list extend the empirical claim to spatial-temporal graph prediction. The introduction also narrows the wording from changes in spatial or temporal input order to changes in spatial order over time. The central claims about permutable memory, input invariance, and general-purpose forecasting remain.

C2.justification: v2 explains moving-versus-static object discovery through the predictive residual, which is disabled for reconstruction, refining v1's distinction between FACTS and SAVi factors. Appendix D additionally qualifies factor-count robustness: reconstruction benefits from sufficient test-time slots, whereas the retained forecasting analysis concerns robustness across separately trained configurations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link and specifies a single NVIDIA A100 GPU with 80 GB memory. Revised Algorithms 1–2 and Appendix C expand documentation of initialization, normalization, predictive residuals, unsupervised-video training, and graph-routing masks. These substantially expand implementation information, although the PDFs do not establish that every newly documented detail represents an implementation change.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds substantive comparisons with Goyal et al.'s factorized recurrent models and SlotSSMs, including a claim that SlotSSMs are a special case under specified conditions. It also positions FACTS within geometric learning and adds the literature supporting graph forecasting and MOVi-A evaluation.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and terminology edits, expands the parallelization explanation, condenses benchmark prose, and moves the former Section 4.3 ablation study into Appendix D. The overall narrative and most introductory, methodological, and theoretical prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds reconstruction and graph-result tables and two diagnostic plots. It rearranges Figure 2 from a two-by-two grid into one row, splits the original object-prediction table across the main text and appendix, relocates ablation tables, and substantially replaces and reorganizes qualitative video panels.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly lacked quantitative comparison for unsupervised object discovery; v2 supplies a matched reconstruction evaluation against SAVi and OC-SlotSSM. Graph forecasting tests the framework's claimed flexibility, while chunk-size and slot-count analyses clarify its behavior. Expanded implementation information and discussion of closely related models further strengthen assessability. New results still lack repeated-run uncertainty, and some original prediction visualizations disappear, but the revision substantially improves the evidence supporting the paper's central claims.
